articles.title: Social Bias or Social Desirability? Comparing Factorial Survey Experiments for Humans and Large Language Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.22409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Factorial survey experiments are a survey method from the social sciences that uses descriptions of socially complex situation (``vignettes'') to elicit judgments such as social bias. They provide two major benefits: (a), they reduce the effect of social desirability inherent in self-reported social biases, and (b), they make it possible to separate the effects of multiple sociodemographic attributes. articles.title: Beyond What Is Visible: Context-Aware Sentiment Across Online Communities Among Crisis Events
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.22551v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Social media offers timely insight into disaster experiences, yet online communities may not represent those affected on the ground. Uneven participation can bias crisis information systems toward data-rich locations and obscure communities with fewer digital traces. articles.title: Generative AI Produces and Transmits Beauty Bias
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.22553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Societies reward people judged to be attractive by standards intertwined with gender and race. In this paper, we examine if and how generative AI may contribute to these dynamics. We audited 27 text-to-image generators released between 2022 and 2026 using simple prompts that never mention attractiveness or beauty, analyzing 51,300 generated faces and 160,196 photographs of real people across primary and supplementary comparisons. articles.title: A misinformation playbook sharpens judgement without breeding cynicism
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.22724v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Misinformation harms public health and democracy, and generative artificial intelligence now writes falsehoods as persuasive as people's. Defences range from fact-checking individual claims to training people to resist falsehoods. Yet many claims are too new to check, and interventions that teach doubt can reduce belief in truth too. We propose a defence that targets not the facts of each claim but the persuasion strategies that recur across them. articles.title: Can AI interview? Comparing AI-led to Human-led Chat Interviews
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.23149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model chatbots have been proposed as AI-interviewers for collecting qualitative interview data at scale, potentially bridging social science's longstanding divide between the breadth of surveys and the depth of qualitative interviews. This paper provides the first direct empirical comparison of data quality in AI-led and human-led interviews. articles.title: Evaluating Predictor-Corrector Dependence in Hard-Constrained Climate Emulators
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.23561v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Climate emulators often enforce physical constraints by correcting each state predicted by a neural network, but evaluating only the corrected forecast conflates predictor skill with the effect of the correction. articles.title: GCAM-Gym: A Benchmark for Agent-Based Climate Policy Search
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.23569v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Comparing climate-policy search methods requires accounting for differences in policy control, available observations, feedback timing, and simulator budgets. We introduce GCAM-Gym, a Gymnasium-compatible environment that supports full-policy evaluation and stepwise control through a common interface and exposes the components of the policy objective. articles.title: A Large Language Model LLM Approach to COVID-19 Fake News Detection
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.23800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Text classification is a widely studied problem in information retrieval and data mining, with applications ranging from healthcare diagnosis to the detection of COVID-19-related fake news.
